workLog.phase: Reproduce the conflict under GitHub's exact condition
actions: Cloned the repo to a scratch path so it carried no git config --local, which is the state GitHub's backend and any CI runner are permanently in
Bound the pre-merge SHAs 2933376d (branch) and 2bad64bc (main at the time) and ran git merge-tree --write-tree
Without the driver: exit 1, CONFLICT (content) in .agents/memory/causality/causal-graph.json, the only conflicting path
With the driver supplied via git -c: exit 0, tree 1dd8e065
workLog.outcome: Confirmed the cause is that .gitattributes names a driver whose definition lives only in git config --local, which is never committed. 1 file changed the outcome.

actions: Built a scratch repo and merged divergent edits under merge=ours, merge=union, merge=binary, text, and an unregistered driver name
merge=ours conflicted, so it is not a git built-in; .gitattributes declares it for .agents/HANDOFF.md and install_merge_drivers.py never registers it
merge=union resolved but concatenated both sides, which yields invalid JSON for a pretty-printed document
Confirmed causal-graph.json is 972992 bytes of pretty-printed JSON with a top-level updated timestamp, not JSONL
workLog.outcome: No git built-in resolves this file correctly, so the custom driver cannot be swapped for a config-free equivalent. 5 cases tested.

workLog.phase: Find where the missing driver actually costs something
actions: Grepped the workflows for runner-side merges: .github/workflows/pr-maintenance.yml runs git merge at two points
Traced .claude/skills/merge-resolver/scripts/resolve_pr_conflicts.py and found _run_git(merge, origin/<target>) at line 345
Read the workflow: it checks out, configures git, then resolves, and escalates blocked files to a paid AI analysis step
Confirmed the job never registers merge drivers and does not use the setup-code-env action
Confirmed scripts/maintenance/install_merge_drivers.py imports only shutil, subprocess, sys and pathlib, computes its own project root, and is idempotent
workLog.outcome: The scheduled maintenance pipeline saw a phantom conflict on nearly every PR and spent model calls on a merge that has a deterministic driver. 2 files changed.

actions: Added a Register git merge drivers step to the process-prs job in .github/workflows/pr-maintenance.yml, after Configure git and before the resolver
Added the same step to .github/actions/setup-code-env/action.yml so any future workflow that merges inherits correct semantics

Re-ran the scratch clone end to end: no driver gave CONFLICT, running the new step verbatim registered the driver and the same merge resolved clean to tree 1dd8e065, byte-identical to the dev-machine result
yaml.safe_load parsed both files and actionlint reported clean
workLog.outcome: Runner-side merges now behave identically to a dev machine, proven by a negative control and a positive case on the same commit pair. 2 files changed.

nextSteps: GitHub computes refs/pull/N/merge in its backend before any runner starts and will never run repository code, so no merge driver can make a PR report MERGEABLE. Closing that half needs option 3 (stop committing the graph) or option 4 (shard it) from issue #3345, both architectural and both requiring the user's decision.

scripts/validation/get_pr_checks equivalent at .claude/skills/github/scripts/pr/get_pr_checks.py has no mergeability awareness, so it reported AllPassing true with 12 checks on PR #3442 where 123 later ran. A conflicting PR should never be able to report all-passing.

.gitattributes declares merge=ours for .agents/HANDOFF.md and merge=handoff-aggregate for .agents/handoffs/*.md. Neither is a git built-in and neither is registered, so both silently fall back to the text merge everywhere.
